leaf.note: bright green glossy keeled blades 0.7-2 cm wide with rough margins

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings on wet mud are small tufts of flat, soft, bright-green leaves; from the first year thick white rhizomes creep out and send up leafy shoots at intervals, so one seedling becomes a spreading, dense bed of broad (1-2 cm) keeled leaves; tall shoots with large open plumes appear from year 2.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Glyceria maxima: highly competitive, invasive rhizomatous perennial grass); Biological Flora of the British Isles (Lambert 1947) and weed-risk accounts (vigorous rhizome spread, germination on wet mud). Values estimated.

traits.leaf_shape: stiff spined sword leaves in a rosette
traits.trunk: none or a short woody stem; tall flower spike
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: grey-green sword leaves 1-3 cm wide with a raised midrib, in flat basal fans

bark.note: stout flower stems; leaf bases flushed pink-brown

growth.juvenile_note: The seedling is a small flat fan of 2-4 narrow, sword-shaped, grey-green leaves rising from a corky floating seed. By the second or third year the rhizome has thickened and branched into several fans of stiff, erect leaves about 1 m tall and the first bright yellow flowers appear; clumps then creep outward on thick rhizomes into dense stands at the water's edge.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Iris pseudacorus: 1-1.5 m, rarely 2 m; flowers 7-10 cm; spreads quickly by rhizome and water-dispersed seed; very wet, even anoxic soils); germination, first flowering and clump ages estimated from rhizomatous iris growth.

leaf.note: oblanceolate, toothed only toward the apex, dotted with yellow resin glands, grey-green

bark.note: dark red-brown smooth stems with pale lenticels and resin glands

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling on wet peat or sandy lake shores; leaves narrowly wedge-shaped, toothed near the tip, grey-green and dotted with fragrant resin glands, as in the adult. It branches from the base into an upright, reddish-brown-twigged little bush and spreads by root suckers into dense clonal thickets; nitrogen-fixing root nodules help it on poor bog soils.
growth.source: Wikipedia Myrica gale (deciduous shrub to 2 m; catkins before the leaves, male yellowish to orange-brown, female red to purple; usually dioecious but plants may change sex from year to year; dense clonal colonies from root suckers); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Myrica (1-6 ft); ages estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (catkins in spring before the leaves, several per twig; red-purple female catkins; small waxy fruits). Here one 'flower' is a female catkin and one 'fruit' the small brown cone-like head it becomes, of 2-3 mm resin-dotted winged nutlets that float off in water; ripe late summer, persists into winter; set and crop estimated
